regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous — until you note that the RBI's own forecast sits 110bps lower at 6.7% YoY, and core sector growth decelerated to 4.8% YoY even as IIP capital goods accelerated to 16.9% YoY. The divergence between infrastructure-adjacent output and the broader eight-sector core is the tell: this is a capex-led expansion with a narrow base. PMI Composite at 55.9 confirms momentum, but passenger vehicle sales falling to 7.9% YoY for a second consecutive month signals that the mass consumer is not yet a participant.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is 44bps above RBI's upper tolerance band, but the composition is what matters: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile reading — and food at 7.74% YoY together explain roughly 60% of the overshoot, while core CPI sits at 3.9% YoY. The inversion: if the RBI treats this as a supply-side shock and holds, it risks embedding fuel costs into wage expectations; if it tightens, it chokes a capex cycle that capacity utilisation at 77.4% is only beginning to justify. WPI at 9.92% YoY means producer margins are being squeezed — that feeds into either lower earnings or higher pass-through within two quarters.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth of 17.8% YoY is a 160bps divergence that has widened for two consecutive months — the CD ratio at 81% sits at the 73rd historical percentile. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-hold cycle was FY14; within four quarters, the RBI was forced into emergency tightening as external pressures compounded domestic funding stress. Today's buffer is larger FX reserves, but NBFC credit accelerating to 15.8% YoY while corporate bond issuance opens as an alternative channel at ₹18,700 cr / month suggests the system is already routing around the constraint — which is precisely when macro-prudential risk weights tend to arrive.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is deteriorating: with CPI at 5.54% YoY, the ex-post real repo rate is effectively negative. The RBI's own inflation forecast has been revised up to 5.1% YoY — 40bps above its prior print — yet the policy stance remains on hold. The second-order effect: a negative real rate with credit growing at 19.4% YoY is an accelerant, not a stabiliser. Housing affordability at 7.25% p.a. average home loan rates is already stretched; any forced tightening to defend the INR or contain inflation would reprice mortgage books and slow the one consumption segment — premium housing — that is currently holding.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), and credit to industry at 18.2% YoY together constitute the most coherent capex signal in several quarters. The threshold that historically triggers private capex acceleration is 75–76% utilisation — we are through it. Manufacturing PMI at 55.1 with new orders expanding confirms demand pull, not just government push. The risk to invert: public sector capex is tracking its FY target, but if fiscal math tightens — fertiliser and fuel subsidy bills are swelling with Brent at $111/bbl — the government's own capex could be the first casualty in H2 FY27.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month sits at the 73rd percentile and is stable, but the composition matters more than the headline: this is a formalization-era GST base, so the question is whether the increment reflects new demand or reclassification of existing informal spend. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural recovery — the informal economy's proxy — while passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY (falling for a second consecutive month) and commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY (also falling two months running) suggest urban discretionary and freight demand are softening. The divergence between two-wheelers and passenger vehicles is the clearest signal that the consumption recovery is bottom-up, not broad-based.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence that has widened for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit, 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY prior), with corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month — a new funding channel opening as banks tighten.","implication":"Banks with CASA ratios below 40% face deposit poaching by larger peers; overweight private banks with CASA > 45%. NBFC funding stress is real — avoid wholesale-dependent NBFCs (>30% of liabilities from bonds/CPs). Expect RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months if credit-deposit gap widens further. Tactical: buy bank bonds maturing 2-3 years (yield pickup on duration risk).","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios >85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19). Current divergence is manageable if deposit growth sustains above 15% YoY.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1% YoY), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), and core sector growth at 4.8% YoY. Manufacturing PMI at 55.1 index (up from 52.8) with new orders and future activity indices both in expansion. Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and credit to services at 24.3% YoY (rising 2 consecutive months) — both signalling capex-led demand. Public sector capex tracking FY target with no slippage reported.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks — order books are filling. Favour companies with 60%+ capex-to-revenue ratios and 12-18 month order visibility. Infrastructure plays (roads, ports, power) will see sustained demand through FY27. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex cycle crowds out consumption. Position for 18-24 month earnings revisions upward in capex-intensive sectors.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at 74th percentile; historically, sustained >76% utilisation preceded 2-3 years of capex acceleration (2003-07, 2014-16). Current momentum is genuine.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, But Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (rising 3 consecutive months: 29,845→31,961→32,297→32,490), at 93rd percentile historically. SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (down from 10.45 mn prior quarter), but SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (up from ₹16.64 lakh cr 3 months ago). Average ticket size implied: ₹17.76 lakh per account (up from ₹15.91 lakh 3 months ago) — a 12% rise in average SIP size. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (up from ₹29,329 cr / month), but NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (down from ₹3,051 cr / month) — retail is rotating into existing schemes, not new launches.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour: affluent money entering via SIP, not mass retail. Existing SIP holders are increasing contributions (ticket size up 12%), signalling confidence but also concentration risk. Avoid new fund launches; existing large-cap and balanced funds will see inflows. Watch for SIP account stagnation — if accounts fall below 9.5 mn while AUM rises, it signals retail saturation. Tactical: overweight large-cap value funds; underweight small-cap NFOs.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile preceded market peaks in 2021 and 2024; rising ticket size is a classic late-cycle signal. Monitor SIP account growth — if it turns negative while AUM grows, expect a correction within 6-12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Import Bill Swelling","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY), at 95th percentile historically. Brent crude at $111.22 / bbl (flat), WTI at $102.51 / bbl (flat), but FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5, rising 2 of last 3 months). India's import-weighted oil basket likely >$110 / bbl. At current crude levels and INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD, India's monthly oil import bill is ~$4.5-5 bn. Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83% YoY) — fuel and food together account for ~60% of the overshoot.","implication":"RBI will struggle to cut rates while fuel inflation remains >20% YoY; expect repo rate to stay at 5.25% p.a. through Q3 FY27. Current account deficit will widen if oil stays >$110 / bbl and INR weakens further. Hedge: long INR forwards (6-12 month), short oil exposure (via crude ETFs or energy stocks). Avoid refiners with weak hedging; favour integrated oil majors. Fiscal pressure on government — expect higher fuel taxes or subsidy cuts by Q4 FY27.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is rare; last seen in 2022 (Ukraine shock) and 2008 (commodity super-cycle). Historically, such levels preceded 200-300 bps of RBI rate hikes over 12-18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Hiking, BOJ Tightening, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a., rising 2 in a row), US 10Y Treasury at 5.05% yield (up from 4.99%, at 91st percentile historically). BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1% p.a., rising 2 in a row, at 100th percentile — highest in 20 years). ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25% p.a., rising 2 in a row). US PMI composite at 58.4 index (rising 2 in a row, at 91st percentile), signalling Fed will hold or hike further. DXY at 101.676 index (flat but up 4 of last 5 months), INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (mild depreciation pressure). FII equity net flows at -₹49,935 cr / month (outflow), reversing prior month's inflow.","implication":"Carry trades (borrow JPY/CHF, invest in INR/emerging markets) are unwinding; expect INR volatility to spike if DXY breaks above 102.5. FII outflows will persist if US rates stay elevated; domestic flows (DIIs at ₹51,829 cr / month net inflow) are insufficient to offset. Tactical: reduce INR-denominated equity exposure; hedge via INR forwards or long USD calls. Avoid high-beta EM assets; rotate to quality (large-cap, dividend-paying). Watch for BOJ policy reversal — if BOJ signals rate cuts, carry unwind accelerates.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 91st percentile and BOJ at 100th percentile is a rare combination; last seen in 2022 (post-Lehman taper tantrum). Historically, such divergence preceded 15-25% EM currency depreciation over 6-12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Holding, But Reserves Pressure Building","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (flat vs prior, but up from 94.34 ₹ / USD 2 months ago — 90 paise depreciation). India VIX at 15.118 index (down from 16.25, at 10th percentile — complacency signal). FII equity net flows at -₹49,935 cr / month (outflow), but DII flows at ₹51,829 cr / month (inflow, at 95th percentile) are masking FII exit. RBI likely intervening to defend INR; FX reserves data not provided, but implied intervention ~$2-3 bn / month based on FII outflows and INR stability.","implication":"RBI's FX reserves are being drawn down to defend INR; this is unsustainable if FII outflows persist. If DII flows weaken (SIP growth slowing, domestic retail saturation), INR will break 96 ₹ / USD within 2-3 months. Tactical: build INR short positions (6-12 month forwards) at current levels; hedge via long USD calls. Monitor RBI's weekly FX reserve data — if reserves fall below $600 bn, expect RBI to signal INR weakness acceptance. Avoid INR-denominated debt; prefer USD-linked returns.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 95.24 is at 89th percentile of weakness; historically, such levels preceded 3-5% further depreciation if external flows turned negative (2013, 2018, 2022).","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surging, But Nifty IT Flat — GCC Decoupling","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter, rising 3 of last 5 quarters), at 7th percentile historically (data sparse, but trend is up). Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (down from 14.74%, falling 2 in a row). Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5%, at 7th percentile — tightest in dataset). Yet Nifty IT index is flat YTD, and IT credit growth at 18.2% YoY (industry-wide) — not accelerating. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6 / sqft / mo (up from ₹102 / sqft / mo), Mumbai at ₹135.8 / sqft / mo (up from ₹130.6 / sqft / mo). Global Capability Centres (GCCs) — captive R&D units of non-IT multinationals — are the primary office absorbers, not traditional IT services firms.","implication":"Commercial real estate is decoupling from IT services stocks. GCCs (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Tesla R&D centres in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune) are the real estate buyers, not TCS/Infosys/Wipro. This means: (1) office rents will rise 8-12% CAGR for next 2-3 years, benefiting REITs (Embassy, MindSpace) and landlords, not IT services; (2) IT services capex is NOT driving office demand — GCC capex is. Tactical: overweight commercial REITs (Embassy at ₹369.92 / unit, MindSpace at ₹345.06 / unit) — both trading below intrinsic value given rent growth. Underweight Nifty IT; the office absorption story is not an IT story. Falsifiable: if IT credit growth accelerates above 25% YoY AND office absorption slows below 10 mn sq ft / quarter, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption data is sparse (7th percentile), but the trend reversal (from 2.6 mn sq ft to 14.1 mn sq ft in 2 quarters) is sharp. Historically, such absorption spikes preceded 3-5 year commercial RE cycles (2015-18, 2019-22). Current cycle is GCC-led, not IT-led — a structural shift.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Consumer Is Splitting in Two

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile), PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) — expansion confirmed across manufacturing and services.
  • But passenger vehicle sales fell to 7.9% YoY for a second consecutive month, and commercial vehicle sales to 12.6% YoY — freight and urban discretionary both decelerating.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural demand recovering — the informal economy's most reliable proxy is moving opposite to the formal consumer.
  • Core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY even as IIP capital goods accelerated to 16.9% YoY — the investment engine is firing; the consumption engine is misfiring by segment.
  • But CPI at 5.54% YoY with fuel at 22.93% YoY is eroding real purchasing power — the mass consumer's fuel bill is the hidden tax on this expansion.

The tension: GDP and PMI signal broad expansion; vehicle sales and core sector tell a narrower story where capex is carrying growth that consumption cannot yet sustain across income segments.

Bottom line: Watch two-wheeler sales as the rural recovery confirmation — a third consecutive month above 25% YoY would validate broadening; a reversal would expose the GDP headline as capex-dependent.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Re-Acceleration on Paper, Real Tightening in the Plumbing

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile), rising two months running — the Fed has no survey-based justification to pause, let alone cut.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.05% yield (91st percentile), up from 4.99% — bond markets are tightening for the Fed; real economy credit costs are already repricing.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in 20 years), rising two consecutive months — yen carry unwind is structural, not episodic.
  • But US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR from 2.2% — nominal growth is running hot, which means the Fed's next move is more likely a hike than a hold.
  • Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY rising two months running, ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. — DM central banks are synchronised tighteners, not diverging.

The tension: Survey data and nominal GDP signal DM re-acceleration, but 10Y yields at 5.05% and BOJ at a 20-year high mean the real tightening is already embedded — the lag to EM flows is 60–90 days, not quarters.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underpriced tail risk for India: each 25bps hike unwinds another layer of yen carry, and FII equity outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month suggest the first wave has already landed.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII Absorption Masking FII Exit — For Now

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising three consecutive months — domestic retail is on structural autopilot.
  • DII equity net inflows at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) are absorbing FII equity outflows of -₹49,935 cr / month almost exactly — the market is balanced on a knife edge.
  • But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) from ₹3,051 cr / month — institutional conviction is absent; retail is rotating into existing schemes, not funding new ideas.
  • MF average AUM fell to ₹87.09 lakh cr from ₹88.31 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion is beginning to show despite SIP inflow strength.
  • India VIX at 15.118 (10th percentile) — complacency is priced in at precisely the moment FII outflows are at a 17th-percentile level of stress.

The tension: SIP inflows and DII absorption are holding the market level, but the NFO collapse and MF AUM decline signal that institutional risk appetite has retreated — the retail bid is structural, the institutional bid is not.

Bottom line: If DII inflows dip below ₹40,000 cr / month while FII outflows persist, the absorption buffer breaks — watch the weekly DII flow print as the primary liquidity signal.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

GCC Boom Absorbed by Office Market, Ignored by REIT Prices

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 18%, +2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY) are the funding source.
  • Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (up 26% from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter), led by GCCs at 41% of occupier mix — Hyderabad absorption surged 92% YoY, NCR 106% YoY.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 10–28% from prior prints — REIT unit prices are pricing IT services stagnation, not GCC expansion.
  • Bengaluru residential: sales 12% YoY, price 8% YoY, only 15 months unsold inventory — the tightest supply-demand balance of any major city.
  • But NCR residential sales turned negative at -1% YoY with launches down 14% YoY — developers are pulling back supply in the market where prices rose 12% YoY, the sharpest divergence in the dataset.

The tension: Office absorption is at multi-year highs driven by GCCs, but REIT prices are pricing IT services — the market has not yet re-rated for the occupier mix shift. Residential is bifurcating sharply by city.

Bottom line: REITs with high GCC tenant exposure (Bengaluru, Hyderabad assets) are mispriced relative to absorption data — watch Q3 REIT distribution announcements for the re-rating catalyst.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Crude Holds the Match

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $111.22/bbl — every $10/bbl adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill; CAD widens ~40bps; INR depreciates 2–3%.
  • FII equity outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month with US 10Y at 5.05% yield and BOJ at 1.25% p.a. — carry unwind is accelerating; INR at 95.24 is holding only on implied RBI intervention.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if deposit growth slips back below 15% YoY, NBFC funding costs reprice within one quarter.
  • India VIX at 15.118 (10th percentile) — complacency at a moment when three independent stress vectors (crude, carry, credit) are simultaneously elevated is itself a risk.
  • But US GDP SAAR at 3.4% SAAR rising two consecutive quarters means the Fed's next move is more likely a hike — a 25bps Fed hike would add 50–75bps to India's effective external funding cost.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; crude at $111/bbl while FII outflows run at -₹49,935 cr / month while the CD ratio sits at 81% is not isolation — it is compounding, and VIX at 10th percentile means the market is not pricing the interaction.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a sustained print above $115/bbl triggers the CAD-INR-inflation feedback loop that forces RBI's hand — that is the threshold that converts a manageable stress into a policy emergency.

"}
